content.title: About
content.content: Flavored iced latte is a cold coffee beverage made with espresso, chilled milk, and a flavored syrup (such as vanilla, caramel, or hazelnut). It is served over ice and offers a smooth, creamy taste with the distinct aroma of the chosen flavor.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Iced latte originated in Japan in the 1990s as a adaptation of the classic latte for hot climates.
Flavor syrups are often made from sugar, water, and natural extracts, though artificial flavors are also common.
The coffee in an iced latte is usually brewed as cold brew or quickly cooled espresso to preserve aroma.
Popular flavors include vanilla, caramel, mint, coconut, and pumpkin.
In some countries the drink is topped with whipped cream or a sprinkle of cinnamon.

items.title: Caffeine boost
items.content: Espresso provides caffeine, which can increase alertness and improve concentration.

items.title: Antioxidant source
items.content: Coffee is rich in polyphenols that help combat free radicals in the body.

items.title: Metabolism support
items.content: Caffeine may slightly raise metabolic rate and aid calorie burning.

items.title: Calcium from milk
items.content: Chilled milk supplies calcium, essential for strong bones and teeth.

items.title: Hydration
items.content: The majority of the drink is water and ice, contributing to daily fluid intake.

items.title: Caffeine sensitivity
items.content: Some individuals may experience anxiety, insomnia, or rapid heartbeat after caffeine consumption.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: Flavored syrups often contain high amounts of sugar, increasing calories and affecting blood glucose levels.

items.title: Lactose intolerance
items.content: Milk can cause discomfort for those who are lactose intolerant; plant‑based milks are viable alternatives.

items.title: Coffee acidity
items.content: The acidity of coffee may irritate the stomach of people with acid reflux or gastritis.

content.title: How to Enjoy
content.content: Serve the iced latte in tall glasses over ice, add a splash of cream or a dusting of cinnamon if desired. Plant‑based milks and sugar‑free syrups can be used to lower calories.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Prepared beverage should be kept in the refrigerator and consumed within 24 hours. Syrups store best in a tightly sealed bottle in a cool place, and milk should remain refrigerated until its use‑by date.
